construct: Neyman bias occurs when a case-control study samples prevalent rather than incident cases and exposure affects both disease occurrence and disease-related survival. Cases who die or recover before sampling are missed, so the exposure distribution among observed cases is distorted.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A case-control study sampling prevalent survivors of a rapidly fatal disease, when exposure increases both disease occurrence and early mortality, preferentially misses exposed fatal cases. This is Neyman, or prevalence-incidence, bias.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Berkson bias requires hospital-admission selection, recall bias requires differential exposure memory, lead-time bias concerns earlier diagnosis and survival time, and observer-expectancy bias concerns measurement influenced by investigators.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Although Neyman bias belongs to the broader family of survivor/selection biases, none of the answer choices is a synonym; the named prevalence-incidence mechanism is uniquely specified.
